title: Enabling Color Picker leaves a blank white window

status.label: Identify the blank window owner
status.detail: Color Picker toggling controls the original rectangle; later sleep/wake reports involve Run and Quick Accent too, so a common cause is not established.

next_action.label: Reproduce startup and wake visibility
next_action.reason: Inspect owning HWND/process and initialization state before choosing a module-local or shared correction.

judgment.rationale: Videos, versions, toggle correlation and an attached ZIP support a focused maintainer test. The linked rounded-corner issue is a different symptom and its release does not prove these persistent blank windows were fixed.
evidence: Original 0.80.1 report shows an immovable empty rectangle that disappears when Color Picker is disabled.
The final comment supplies a ZIP and identifies two sleep/wake rectangles disappearing when Run and Quick Accent are toggled.
Related #31725 concerns dropper corner/background rendering and says its fix shipped in 0.82.0; this report continued afterward.
Current ColorPickerXAML/App.xaml.cs creates an overlay described as initially hidden; reproducing a visible helper window requires runtime ownership evidence.
judgment.recommended_action: Trace window creation/show/hide for each reproducible owner, then approve only the demonstrated lifecycle correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: An initialization/visibility correction may apply, but no reviewed fix specifically covers persistent white windows across these modules.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent an uninitialized helper overlay from becoming visible
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a module helper window becomes visible before transparent content/hidden state is fully established, or is incorrectly restored after wake. Later Run/Quick Accent rectangles may be separate defects rather than the same Color Picker path.
plan: Reproduce the Color Picker enable/disable case and inspect the blank HWND's owning process, styles and show/restore transitions; repeat the wake case with one module enabled at a time.

For a confirmed Color Picker owner, trace App.OnLaunched and ColorPickerOverlayWindow initialization in src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/ColorPickerXAML; compare the affected historical build with the current overlay implementation.

Correct the demonstrated visibility transition so helper windows remain hidden until intentionally activated and do not show empty content after resume; do not apply a broad shared fix without matching evidence.
Add cold-start, repeated enable/disable and sleep/resume tests for the confirmed owner, preserving hotkey activation and normal dismissal.
verification: No persistent blank rectangle remains after starting PowerToys or toggling Color Picker; normal picker hotkey interaction still works.
After sleep/resume, inspect Color Picker, Run and Quick Accent separately and verify the candidate fixes only the demonstrated owner without hiding legitimate UI.

confidence.rationale: Module toggling narrows ownership, but the report combines different processes and current Color Picker uses a changed overlay implementation; no runtime trace confirms the lifecycle branch.

issue_context.summary: A persistent white helper window correlates with Color Picker enablement; later reports describe similar rectangles from Run and Quick Accent after waking the PC.
known_information: The original report provides a recording and a deterministic module-toggle correlation.
Multiple versions and an additional screenshot/ZIP are already supplied.
The linked rounded-dropper report #31725 is closed and marked released in 0.82.0, yet this issue has later occurrences.
Live issue is open and unassigned.
inferences: An unintended visible helper-window state is plausible; a shared multi-module root cause is unproven.
issue_context.analysis: Do not request the recording or diagnostics already present. A maintainer should establish HWND/process ownership and whether current code still fails before designing a specific visibility fix.
initial_investigation: Read all comments, the related #31725 report, timeline-linked duplicates and matching PR search.
Inspected upstream ColorPickerXAML/App.xaml.cs overlay initialization; no claim is made to have analyzed the attached ZIP.

actions.label: Identify blank HWND during enable and wake

reproduce.module: Color Picker; separately PowerToys Run and Quick Accent
reproduce.version: Current stable build; historical reports 0.80.1 through 0.84.1
prerequisites: Use a window-inspection tool to identify HWND, PID and visibility styles.
Test one module at a time before testing combinations.
steps: Start with Color Picker disabled, enable it without invoking the hotkey and look for a persistent white window.
Identify the owning process and HWND, then disable Color Picker and confirm whether that HWND disappears.
Repeat cold launch and sleep/resume while tracing creation/show/hide events.
Repeat separately for Run and Quick Accent using the final comment's toggle workaround.
Invoke each module normally to distinguish a helper-window artifact from legitimate module UI.
reproduce.expected_result: Idle modules leave no blank visible helper windows; any reproduced rectangle is attributed to its actual owning process before changing code.

actions.label: Approve owner-specific visibility investigation
actions.note: Low-confidence plan; establish the process and failing transition before implementing.
